name: Unit 7 - Galen System Focused Review - GI Student

slides.title: Function of GI Tract
text: Absorption of nutrients produced by digestion into bloodstream
Elimination of undigested foods and other waste products

slides.title: Upper GI Series
text: Barium – radiopaque, tasteless, odorless, insoluble; fluoroscopy
Involves the esophagus, stomach, small intestine
Wall thickness, motility/emptying, mucosal pattern, patency of pyloric valve, etc.
Dx – ulcers, varices, tumors, regional enteritis, malabsorption
Pre: Low residue diet, NPO after midnight, laxative
Post: Push fluids, stools clay colored

slides.title: Lower GI Series
text: Barium enema: examine anatomy, function detect polyps, tumors, lesions of lg intestine
Instillation of thick barium followed by air; cramping
Pre: low residue diet, clear liquid diet; NPO after midnight; enemas till clear; schedule before UGI
Contraindicated if active inflammation, perforation, obstruction

slides.title: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy(EGD)
text: Fiber optic; esophageal, gastric, duodenal abnormalities
Client sedated IV midazolam (Versed), topical anesthetics; approx. 30 min
Pre: NPO 6 –12 hours before; atropine (secretions); glucagon (relax smooth muscle)
Left lateral to facilitate saliva drainage, passage of scope; monitor VS
Post: NPO till gag reflex; monitor for s/s perforation; oral anesthetics prn

slides.title: Colonoscopy
text: Left lateral, legs drawn toward chest; reposition prn; approx. 1 hour
Discomfort from air instillation, scope movement
Monitor cardiac & respiratory status cont. r/t medications given, vagal stim., hydration
Pre: Limit fluids 24 – 48 hours, Fleets/saline enemas till clear; informed consent
- Polyethylene glycol electrolyte lavage sol. (Golytely, Colyte, NuLytely) on ice, over 3 – 4 hours
- SE; nausea, bloating, cramps, fullness, FE imbalance

slides.title: Do not take routine meds during lavage; meds won't be absorbed
text: Do not take routine meds during lavage; meds won't be absorbed
Clients w/ DM need med adjustments r/t dietary changes for test
Maintain adequate fluid, electrolyte, caloric intake
DC NSAIDs before & 2 weeks after procedure; other anticoagulants

slides.title: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease
text: Chronic backflow of gastric contents into esophagus
Incompetent LES, pyloric stenosis, motility disorder
Diagnosed by  endoscopy or barium swallow
Avoid food & fluids 2 hours before HS
What foods do we educate GERD clients to avoid?

slides.title: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease
text: Blocks action of histamine on histamine receptors of parietal cells
Proton (gastric acid) Pump Inhibitors ( end in –zole)
Decrease acid secretion slows H+, K+ ATP pump on parietal cell surface

slides.title: Peptic Ulcer Disease (PUD)
text: H.pylori associated with development gastric (pylorus), duodenal (frequent), esophageal
40 - 60 your old; often men & postmenopausal women
Dull, gnawing pain, burning sensation in mid epigastrium

slides.title: Duodenal vs.  Gastric Ulcers
text: Pain worse with food (if penetrating ulcer)
What medications would these clients receive?

slides.title: Occurs after gastric surgery
text: Rapid passage of food into jejunum & drawing of fluid into jejunum due to hypertonic intestinal contents

slides.title: Diverticulitis
text: Diverticulum – saclike outpouching of the mucosa in the colon
Diverticulosis – multiple diverticula present without inflammation
Diverticulitis – food & bacteria retained in diverticula produce infection & inflammation
Asymptomatic until complications( fistulas, abscesses, obstructions, hemorrhage)

slides.title: Diverticulitis
text: Acute pain in left lower quadrant
Abscess formation: tenderness, palp mass, fever, leukocytosis
Perforation: abd pain localized over segment; often sigmoid
Peritonitis: abd pain, rigid board like abd

slides.title: Crohn's Disease
text: Common in women, teens to 30 years of age
Transmural from mucosa to bowel wall (all layers)
Edema, thickening of mucosa, ulcerated areas
Cobblestone appearance, thickening & fibrosis of bowel wall, narrowed lumen

slides.title: Ulcerative Colitis
text: Recurrent ulcerative & inflammation of mucosal & submucosal layers of colon, rectum
Stool hemoccult  (+), low Hgb & Hct, increased WBC, low albumin, electrolyte imbalance

slides.title: Treatment for Crohn's & Ulcerative Colitis
text: Tx aimed at attaining normal elimination patterns

slides.title: Gallbladder
text: 3 – 4” hollow, long, pear shaped, smooth muscle tissue, stores bile
- Bile produced by liver; breaks down fats
Attached to underside of liver via connective tissue
Cystic duct joins common hepatic duct, forms common bile duct; terminates in duodenum
Fatty foods - gallbladder contracts - sphincter of Oddi (stopper at gallbladder neck) opens  - bile released into duodenum

slides.title: Cholelithiasis AKA Calculous/Gallstones
text: Incidence increases w/ age; common > 40 years old
Pigment stones: unconjugated pigments in bile precipitate form stones
Cholesterol: normal bile constituent; supersaturation of bile w/ cholesterol; irritates
Women 4x > men, multiparous, > 40 years, obese, oral contraceptives
Epigastric distress after fried/fatty meal, vague pain in RUQ

slides.title: Management of Cholelithiasis
text: Acute: rest, IV fluids, NG suction, analgesics, antibiotics
Dietary management: low fat, avoid ETOH
Medications: ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) and chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA)
Dissolve cholesterol calculi; 6 –12 month treatment used for poor surgical candidates

slides.title: Pancreas
text: Pancreatic duct joins common bile duct – enters duodenum at ampulla of Vater
Sphincter of Oddi partially controls rate of secretions entering

slides.title: Acute Pancreatitis
text: Activation of pancreatic enzymes inside the pancreas instead of the intestines
Severe acute abdominal pain( LUQ) due to irritation and edema
Serum amylase, serum lipase levels elevate

slides.title: Chronic Pancreatitis
text: Recurring attacks of severe upper abd & back pain with vomiting
Steatorrhea – frequent, frothy, foul smelling stools r/t impaired fat & protein absorption
Persistent unrelieved pain difficult to manage (Can give morphine)
Limit ETOH & avoid foods (fats) that exacerbate

slides.title: Liver Functions
text: Metabolizes bilirubin; by-product of destruction of senescent RBCs
Synthesizes vit. K , fibrinogen, prothrombin, other clotting factors

slides.title: Liver Function Studies
text: Pigment studies: direct/indirect serum bilirubin, urine bilirubin, and urine bilirubin, urobilinogen

slides.title: Portal Hypertension
text: Obstructed blood flow causes increased pressure t/o portal venous system

slides.title: Hepatic Encephalopathy & Coma
text: A life-threatening complication of liver disease
- Results from accumulation of ammonia and other toxic metabolites in blood
- Increased ammonia in blood causes brain dysfunction
Changes in level of consciousness; assess neurologic status frequently
Fetor hepaticus; sweet/fecal odor; fresh mowed grass, acetone, old wine
Monitor fluid, electrolyte, and ammonia levels

slides.title: Hepatitis
text: Inflammation of the liver caused by a virus

slides.title: Cirrhosis
text: Chronic progressive degeneration and destruction of liver cells

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Question
text: The nurse is preparing to teach an in-service for nursing staff about post operative care for the client following abdominal surgery. Which content should the nurse speak about in the in-service? Select all that apply.
“Therapeutic touch is an effective way to decrease postoperative abdominal pain.”
“Total body relaxation is an effective adjunct for postoperative pain management.”
“The nursing process is linear throughout the postoperative care of clients who have had abdominal surgery.”

“The nurse’s priority is to check on the client who had abdominal surgery and returned to the unit just now and then check on the client who is requesting pain medication and returned from abdominal surgery 12 hours ago.”

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Question
text: The nurse is preparing to teach an in-service for nursing staff and students about total parenteral nutrition. Which information should the nurse include in the in-service? Select all that apply.
“Clients with paralytic ileus or severe diarrhea are candidates for parenteral nutrition.”
“Total parenteral nutrition is delivered for the client through a gastrostomy or nasogastric tube.”
“Protein, electrolyte, and glucose nutritional imbalances may be supplemented with total parenteral nutrition.”
“Clients who need long-term nutritional supplementation will receive total parenteral nutrition via IV solutions comprised of 5% dextrose.”
